title: A-R-V
hook: erev, evening; arev, sweet, and a guarantor: all Israel are guarantors

segments.voice: Yesterday, Sh-Ch-R: shachar, the first light, and Shacharit, the morning prayer. Your line was dawn. Did you catch it? Today, the other end of the day, and two more meanings in the same letters. Day one thousand four hundred twenty.

A father refuses to send his youngest son down to Egypt. He has already lost one boy; he won't risk Benjamin. But the family is running out of food. Then Judah, an older brother, steps forward: "I will be surety for him; of my hand shalt thou require him." Put him on my account. If he doesn't come back, the blame is mine. Later, in Egypt, when Benjamin is about to be kept as a slave, Judah steps forward again and offers to stay in his place. Today's root is the word under surety.
screen: `A FATHER WON'T SEND BENJAMIN.` → `I WILL BE SURETY FOR HIM.` → `LET ME STAY INSTEAD.`

segments.voice: A-R-V. Ayin, resh, vet. These letters carry more than one meaning, so turn them a few ways. First, evening. Erev. The Torah's first day ends with it: "And the evening and the morning were the first day." Evening is named before morning, and the rabbis read that as the reason a Jewish day, Shabbat included, begins in the evening. Second, sweet. Arev. A psalm says, "My meditation of him shall be sweet." And the blessing said before studying Torah asks God to make its words sweet in our mouths, with a word from these letters. Third, the guarantor. Arev again: the one who stands surety, the way Judah did for his brother. The Talmud puts it in a single line: kol Yisrael arevim zeh ba-zeh, all Israel are guarantors for one another. In its setting it explains how one person can bear responsibility for another's wrong. In its widest reading it says that nobody in the community is only on their own account. Fourth, side by side. These may be separate words that happen to share a spelling. Some teachers set them together anyway: a day that begins in the dark, words that taste sweet, and people who answer for each other. Judah's surety is where it gets concrete. He didn't promise to feel responsible. He put himself in the place where Benjamin would have stood.
screen: `EREV: EVENING COMES FIRST.` · `AREV: SWEET IN THE MOUTH.` · `AREV: THE ONE WHO STANDS SURETY.` · `ALL ISRAEL ARE GUARANTORS.` · then, large: `WE STAND SURETY.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: take responsibility for someone. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind one person whose life touches yours: a child, a parent, a neighbor, a coworker who's struggling, a friend who's gone quiet. See yourself standing next to them, the way Judah stood beside his brother. Then ask one question: where could I put my name beside theirs this week? Vouching for them. Going with them to a hard appointment. Speaking up for them in a room they aren't in. Choose one, and hold it in mind. If you pray, you can pray for them by name. The bell holds the time.
screen: `ONE PERSON.` · `STAND BESIDE THEM.` · `PUT YOUR NAME BESIDE THEIRS.`

segments.voice: A-R-V. Ayin, resh, vet: erev, evening; arev, sweet; and arev, the one who stands surety. Today's word.
Your line: we stand surety. Today, do one thing for someone as if their outcome were on your account. Day one thousand four hundred twenty.

howItsDone: Jewish days, Shabbat and festivals begin at evening, read from Genesis 1:5; the blessing before Torah study asks that its words be sweet; and the Talmud's principle 'all Israel are guarantors for one another' (Shevuot 39a) is cited for mutual responsibility.

fork.setup: you're Judah. in Egypt, the governor says Benjamin must stay behind as a slave. what do you do?
options: go home and tell your father the news.
offer to stay as a slave in Benjamin's place.

fork.reveal: "thy servant became surety for the lad": Judah asks to stay instead, so the boy can go home to his father.

original.note: Hebrew: a guarantor, one who stands surety; the same spelling means sweet, and erev, evening, shares the letters.

trapdoor: what you thought: erev just means evening, as in erev Shabbat.
what it means: the same letters give evening, sweet, and the guarantor who answers for someone else.
what a scholar hears: Shevuot 39a, kol Yisrael arevim zeh ba-zeh, read from a verse about people stumbling one over another.

notes: Genesis 43:9 anochi e'ervenu; 44:32 arav et ha-na'ar. Confirm.
Genesis 1:5: the rabbinic reading that the day begins with evening (e.g., Berakhot 2a and commentators). Phrased 'the rabbis read that as the reason'. Confirm.
Psalm 104:34 ye'erav; Birkat HaTorah v'ha'arev na. Confirm.
Shevuot 39a: kol Yisrael arevim zeh ba-zeh, derived from Leviticus 26:37 ('they shall stumble one upon another', read as one for the sin of another). Confirm context summary.
The script says linguists discuss whether erev / arev (sweet) / arev (surety) are one root or homonyms; no position taken. Confirm.
Index pairs 'arev, sweet, and a guarantor'; the script keeps both.
